relationships.subject: ASIC3
relationships.evidence_quote: conditional knockout of Asic3 in proprioceptors (Pv-Cre::Asic3f/f) substantially reduced the development of chronic hyperalgesia

relationships.subject: proprioceptors
relationships.evidence_quote: Collectively, these results indicate that only activated Pv-positive proprioceptors, but not Nav1.8-positive nociceptors, contribute to the hyperalgesic priming.

relationships.subject: PCCG-13
relationships.evidence_quote: it dose-dependently inhibited the acid injection-induced chronic hyperalgesia in the Pv-Cre::LMO3 mice

relationships.subject: substance P
relationships.evidence_quote: inhibited the hyperalgesic priming and development of chronic hyperalgesia by a follow-up acid challenge in Pv-Cre::LMO3 mice

key_findings: ASIC3 in Pv-positive proprioceptors, not Nav1.8 nociceptors, is required for acid-induced chronic hyperalgesia in mouse chronic widespread pain models.
Proprioceptor activation primes hyperalgesia via GluK2 signaling and is blocked by substance P (NK1); in humans intramuscular acid evokes soreness (sng) distinct from pain.
